title: World only, or the opening too
statement: A film before a reading may show only the setting, or also the characters and the plot's opening: one rule bans plot, but previews measured to help included it.
detail: One version of the intro-video rules shows only the world and none of the plot, "even when revealing plot would measurably improve comprehension" (`downloads/BrainLift - What makes a good intro video.md`, line 41). The other says a video that shows only scenery has built atmosphere rather than knowledge and missed the mark (line 291), and notes that the previews measured in the research contained plot, so a blanket ban is a position nobody has tested (line 422). The study it cites found that previews of the characters plus the opening of the plot produced sizeable comprehension gains, largest for lower-ability readers (line 447; Graves, Cooke and Laberge 1983).
against: The world-only version calls itself internal doctrine, with no child yet observed watching one of its films (`downloads/BrainLift - What makes a good intro video.md`, line 249).
